name: Chart View
tagline: A Dataverse view as a bar, column, pie, donut or line chart — grouped by a column, aggregated on the server.
summary:
Draws a Dataverse view as a column, bar, pie, donut or line chart on a form, a main grid or a canvas screen: one mark per distinct value of the column you group by, counting the records in each group or adding up a number column.

- On a model-driven app the numbers come from one aggregate over the whole view, not the loaded page, and the caption says which
- Groups by a choice, yes/no, lookup or text column, or by a date bucketed by day, week, month, quarter or year
- Pressing a bar or a slice reports the group that was clicked as an output

limitations: The server route — one aggregate over the whole view — cannot run here. It reads the view's own definition (savedquery, or userquery for a personal view) and sends one FetchXML aggregate; the demo's stand-in Dataverse has no views and answers no FetchXML, so both reads are refused, as the event log shows, and the chart groups the fixture's rows in the browser, the route a canvas app takes. Switch the toolbar's host to Canvas app and the chart takes that route without asking the server at all. With sixteen rows on one page the numbers are the same a server would return.

Industry's colours come from its options, which the stand-in Dataverse describes with a colour each, read through getEntityMetadata as on a model-driven form; the blank group takes a neutral grey. Sorting by label follows the options' own order — the order the maker gave them — which Bars in the category's own order shows.
The fixture holds Industry as option values, as Dataverse does, and the chart labels each group from the options.
Clicking a group sets the two outputs, which the harness shows in its property panel; nothing on the demo page consumes them.
